record.body:
## Rationale

A repeated failure is a reason to look one level higher only when the new check adds nothing and the cause is still the one already named. The first implementation failure still returns to execute. The next assessment stays on execute when a new evidence kind, a narrower failing case, or a newly named cause shows up. Otherwise it raises `implementation` to `design`, and `design` to `specification`. `plan` and `integration` are chosen when the evidence says the decomposition or the composition is the problem. They are not steps a counter walks through. At `specification`, with still no new evidence, the loop asks the user.

## Counter-argument

A count of three is easy to test and easy to explain. After three failed assessments the loop would stop sending the same task back to execute, so a stuck agent cannot spin. The count does not know whether the third run learned anything, and it turns an implementation failure into a design failure by arithmetic.

payload.alternatives: A fixed count of three failed assessments, which then blocks or relabels the failure as a design problem.
payload.choice: A repeated assessment stays at the same level only when evidence increased or the cause was resolved. Otherwise raise one step: implementation, then design, then specification. Plan and integration are direct diagnoses.
